items.headline: Russian Court Bars Anti-War Yabloko Party From Parliamentary Election
items.summary: Russia's Supreme Court ruled on Monday to bar Yabloko, the only registered political party opposing the conflict in Ukraine, from next month's parliamentary elections [1.3.5]. The decision disqualifies the nation's primary anti-war opposition group from the ballot following a legal challenge by a pro-Kremlin party.

items.headline: NASA Extends Voyager 2 Spacecraft Mission with Power-Saving Maneuver
items.summary: NASA engineers executed a clever power-saving operation nicknamed the Big Bang to extend the operational lifespan of the Voyager 2 probe. By shutting down non-essential components and switching to lower-power alternatives, the team bought the nearly 50-year-old spacecraft at least another year of scientific data collection in interstellar space.

items.headline: Jakob Ingebrigtsen Wins European 5,000-Meter Gold in Thrilling Comeback
items.summary: Norwegian runner Jakob Ingebrigtsen claimed his fourth consecutive 5,000-meter title at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham after surging past competitors in the final 50 meters. The victory marks a triumphant return for the two-time Olympic champion, who was competing in his first race since undergoing Achilles tendon surgery earlier this year.

items.headline: Jury Selection Begins in Las Vegas Trial for 1996 Killing of Tupac Shakur
items.summary: Jury selection officially began in Las Vegas for the trial of Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, who faces murder charges in connection with the 1996 shooting of rap icon Tupac Shakur. The landmark proceedings mark a major milestone in seeking legal resolution for one of hip-hop's most famous cold cases nearly thirty years later.
